key_insight: Reactive machine learning simulations identify two friction regimes at diamond–silicon nitride interfaces: bond-density-controlled interfacial sliding and shear within the softer material under full interfacial bonding.
engineering_relevance: Controlling diamond surface passivation, orientation and load could help manage friction and wear in ceramic contacts and polishing processes.
method: Train a reactive C/H/N/O/Si interatomic potential on diverse bulk, surface, interface and molecular structures.
Test diamond reaction barriers and amorphous silicon nitride and silica structural/mechanical properties.
Simulate diamond–silicon nitride sliding across four diamond orientations, clean and H/OH-passivated surfaces, and loads of 0.1–23 GPa.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation against ab initio reaction barriers and ceramic properties, but provides no numerical prediction errors.
watch_item: Transferability to realistic wear and polishing conditions remains to be established beyond the reported sliding simulations.
paper_title: Development and application of a machine learning potential for diamond surfaces and their sliding interfaces with silicon nitride and silica: effect of passivation, orientation and load
